title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias
abstract: arXiv:2606.19544v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLM-as-a-Judge has become the dominant evaluation paradigm for language models, but judge validation in practice relies on exact-match agreement, a metric that does not correct for chance and systematically overstates discriminative ability. We present the largest systematic evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge to date: 21 judges from nine providers across MT-Bench, JudgeBench, and RewardBench, evaluated under three protocols (agreement, consistency, bias audit) over 118 runs and approximately 541,000 individual judgments. Four findings emerge, consistent across the full cohort, including the April 2026 frontier: kappa deflation between exact match and Cohen's kappa is universal (33--41 pp on MT-Bench), judge rankings shift by up to 14 positions across benchmarks, high test--retest reliability (>0.95) coexists with severe position bias (>0.10) in two production-deployed judges (instantiating a consistency--bias paradox), and verbosity bias i

translated_title: 无有效性的可靠性：对LLM-as-a-Judge（大语言模型作为评判者）模型在一致性、稳定性和偏见方面的系统性大规模评估
translated_abstract: LLM-as-a-Judge已成为语言模型评估的主导范式，但实践中的评判者验证依赖于精确匹配一致率这一指标，该指标既未对随机巧合进行校正，又系统性地高估了评判者的判别能力。我们呈现了迄今最大规模的LLM-as-a-Judge系统性评估：来自九家提供商的21个评判者模型，涵盖MT-Bench、JudgeBench和RewardBench三个基准，在三种协议（一致性、稳定性、偏见审计）下进行了118次运行和约541,000次单独评判。四项发现贯穿整个评测队列（包括2026年4月的前沿模型）：精确匹配与Cohen's kappa之间的kappa衰减是普遍现象（在MT-Bench上达33–41个百分点）；评判者排名在不同基准之间偏移多达14个位置；在两个已部署于生产环境的评判者中，高重测信度（>0.95）与严重的位置偏见（>0.10）并存（构成一个稳定性—偏见悖论）；此外还有冗长偏见……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究对来自九家提供商的21个LLM评判者进行了迄今最大规模的系统性评估，发现精确匹配一致率普遍系统性高估评判能力（kappa衰减33–41个百分点）、评判者排名跨基准偏移可达14位、且高稳定性与严重偏见可并存，证明可靠性并不等于有效性。
en_tdlr: The largest systematic evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge models shows that exact-match agreement systematically overstates judge quality—kappa deflation is universal, rankings shift up to 14 positions across benchmarks, and high consistency coexists with severe bias—demonstrating that reliability does not imply validity.
